item.title: Federal Report Says Firefighting Tactics Aided Blast at Maine Lumber Mill
item.description: Firefighters who responded to a fire at a Maine lumber mill used tactics that inadvertently contributed to a massive explosion that killed three people, according to a report from federal investigators. The fire companies tried to extinguish the May 15 fire inside a silo at the Robbins Lumber mill in rural Searsmont, Maine, by injecting it with water — unaware of warnings from the manufacturer that doing so would be dangerous. “The application of water into the silo in this incident likely entrained oxygen into the silo headspace, stirred up dust within the contents, and caused it to become suspended in an explosive concentration.” The report recommends that fire departments ensure firefighters choose appropriate tactics for silo fires and never direct water or foam into oxygen-limiting silos.

item.title: U.S. Forecaster Predicts More Than 90% Risk of a Strong El Niño
item.description: El Niño is strengthening, with a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter 2026-27, the U.S. A powerful El Niño weather event could push nearly 49 million more people into acute food insecurity across some of the world’s most vulnerable regions by the end of next year, the World Food Programme said earlier this month. “During the October-December 2026 season, there is a 69% chance of a historic event that would exceed the strength of previous El events dating back to 1950,” the weather forecaster added.

item.title: After Drop Last Year, Car Insurance Rates Climb: Insurify
item.description: After a 6% drop in 2025, car insurance rates are projected to climb back in more than half the nation, with 27 states posting increases in the first half of 2026, according to Insurify’s 2026 Mid-Year Auto Report. While rates are rising in some historically inexpensive states for car insurance, three of the most expensive states bucked the early-year trend, highlighting rate decreases. By the end of the year, 32 states are expected to see rate increases, according to Insurify’s data projections.

item.title: GIC Re sees increased profit and gross premium income in Q1’27
item.description: General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re), the Indian public sector reinsurer, has announced its latest financial results, reporting increased profit after tax and gross premium income of ₹1,922.04 and ₹13,475.36 crore, respectively, for the first quarter ending June 30, 2026. Gross premium income in the quarter compares to the ₹12,388.01 crore seen in Q1 2026. Q1 2027 profit after tax was up from the ₹1,752.23 crore reported for the same period the year prior.

item.title: New data creates opportunity for insurers to protect properties more effectively against wildfires: Cotality
item.description: It shows that new data and analytic capabilities create an opportunity to protect properties more effectively in the evolving wildfire environment we’re facing. New property-level data reveals how fire spreads between homes, offering insurers and homeowners a critical opportunity to identify extra steps that can be taken to reduce risk and enhance resilience, according to a recent Cotality report. Cotality’s 2026 Wildfire Risk Report found that over 2.5 million properties across the 10 most exposed states in the west of the United States carry a moderate or greater risk of wildfire, representing a combined reconstruction cost value (RCV) of nearly $1.4 trillion.

item.title: Reports suggest Colombia quake will drive insured losses across multiple lines in LatAm market
item.description: Higher earthquake insurance penetration in Colombia is expected to mean the magnitude 7.4 quake that struck the country will generate an insured loss for the wider Latin American insurance market, according to global reinsurance broker Guy Carpenter, a Marsh business. AM Best, the global credit rating agency, has also commented on the earthquake, saying that it’s expected to drive claims across multiple lines of insurance business, notably from commercial and residential property. While the physical consequences of the event are still being assessed, the company’s market analysis indicates that Colombia’s comparatively higher level of earthquake insurance coverage is likely to make the event more significant for insurers and reinsurers across the region.

item.description: Severe weather cut power to more than half a million people in the Chicago area and northwestern Indiana as perilous thunderstorms and tornadoes pummeled the region Tuesday, causing widespread damage and bringing lightning that injured people at an Ohio prison. The weather service bluntly warned earlier in the day: “These are dangerous storms!” More than 600,000 customers lost electricity in Illinois and Indiana, according to poweroutage.us. Tornado warning sirens howled as the skies darkened.

item.title: Dallas-Based Bus Companies Settle Allegations of PPP Loan Violations for $3.9M
item.description: and El Expreso Group, LLC, two affiliated Dallas-based bus companies that operate numerous international bus routes between the United States and Mexico, agreed to pay $3.9 million to resolve allegations that the companies violated the False Claims Act by applying for and receiving loans that they were not eligible for in the Small Business Administration’s Paycheck Protection Program (PPP), announced United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould. Congress created the PPP in March 2020, as part of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief and Economic Security (CARES) Act to provide emergency loans to small businesses suffering economic hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Tornado Bus and El Expreso applied for and received PPP loans in the combined principal amount of approximately $2.8 million in 2021, which loans were later forgiven in full.

item.title: Mandarin Re raises capital as reinsurer retreat opens market gaps
item.description: Labuan-based Mandarin Re has raised its paid-up capital to $26 million, its second capital increase this year, as it looks to expand into markets where larger reinsurers have reduced their presence. The additional capital supports Mandarin Re’s target of writing $70 million in gross written premium in 2026 , according to the company. Mandarin Re said the move comes as larger reinsurers concentrate capital on core markets and withdraw from some secondary territories as pricing conditions soften.

item.title: How A Teenage Carpenter Became The Founder Of AI Construction Startup Trunk Tools
item.description: Before founding Trunk Tools , an AI startup for the construction industry, Sarah Buchner spent more than a decade working in construction. While doing that research, she realized something that would later become central to Trunk Tools: Construction companies produce huge amounts of information, but much of it is fragmented across different systems and buried in documents, making it difficult to analyze. item.title: August 9th – 11th US Midwest SCS outbreak may rank as a top-10 industry loss: Guy Carpenter
item.description: Multiple rounds of severe thunderstorm activity that struck the Midwest of the United States earlier this month is seen as having the potential to result in a top-10 severe weather insurance industry loss event, which implies that the cost could be around $5.1 billion or higher to the market, according to broker Guy Carpenter. Guy Carpenter also commented on the potential financial impacts of this severe thunderstorm outbreak in the United States, “Given the severity of winds in the Chicago, Indianapolis, and Columbus, OH metropolitan areas, insured losses are likely to be measured in the billions of dollars.” The broker added: “It is plausible given initial reports of damage that the last several days of severe weather activity could breach the top ten list.” Guy Carpenter’s ranking of the top-10 severe convective storm insured loss events in the United States since 1995 can be seen below: At the bottom of that list is a $5.1 billion industry insured loss event from May 2014. Between August 9th to 11th, the Midwest was impacted by multiple rounds of severe convective storm (SCS) activity, driven by a slow-moving cold front affecting the states of Wisconsin, Illinois, Iowa, Indiana, Ohio, as well as other surrounding states.

item.title: Liberty Mutual Re makes sensor-triggered parametric earthquake payout in Peru
item.description: Liberty Mutual Reinsurance (LM Re), part of Liberty Mutual Insurance Group, has issued a parametric payout for the 5.8 magnitude earthquake that struck Peru in May and activated Safehub’s Shake Network trigger. The policy, which is being dubbed by both companies as the world’s first earthquake parametric payment triggered by Safehub’s Shake Network uses ShakeNet Parametric, Liberty Mutual Re’s (LM Re) earthquake parametric solution that is triggered by Safehub’s, a provider of seismic sensor and risk management technology. Powered by the Global Earthquake Model’s (GEM’s) OpenQuake engine, and informed by Safehub’s sensor network, the parametric solution delivers highly localised shaking information that supports rapid, transparent, and objective payouts while enhancing emergency response and post-event decision-making.

item.title: PERILS reduces storm Nils insured market loss estimate to €695m
item.description: Catastrophe data aggregator PERILS has published its third industry loss estimate for extratropical windstorm Nils, also known as “Ulrike”, that struck the Nouvelle-Aquitaine and Occitanie regions in southwest France in mid-February, placing the insurance market loss at €695 million, a notable decline from its second estimate that was published in May. PERILS confirmed that it will provide an updated loss estimate for Nils on February 13th, 2027, twelve months after the event end date. PERILS published its initial insurance industry loss estimate for this windstorm back in March, putting the total at €586 million.

item.title: Accelerant heads back to private ownership with Thoma Bravo acquisition
item.description: Upon completion, Accelerant will become a private company, with its common shares delisted from the New York Stock Exchange, while Altamont Capital Partners, its largest investor, and the firm’s founders intend to retain equity alongside Thoma Bravo, with the terms to be finalised prior to closing. Data-driven risk exchange platform Accelerant has entered into a definitive agreement with Thoma Bravo to become a privately held company in an all-cash transaction with an enterprise value of more than $4 billion. The move marks a strategic return to the private market for Accelerant, highlighting how public markets have at times struggled to properly assess and value tech-enabled, specialty risk exchange platforms over short-term quarters.

item.title: Midwest severe storms could generate billions in insured losses, Guy Carpenter warns
item.description: A severe convective storm outbreak that swept across the US Midwest between August 9 and 11 could generate insured losses running into the billions of dollars, according to a recent report from Guy Carpenter. The firm added, “It is plausible given initial reports of damage that the last several days of severe weather activity could breach the top ten largest US severe convective storm insured losses list.” The latest outbreak follows a substantial severe weather event in the Midwest in late July, which was also identified as having the potential to become a top-10 US severe convective storm insured loss event. “Given the severity of winds in the Chicago, Indianapolis, and Columbus, OH metropolitan areas, insured losses are likely to be measured in the billions of dollars,” Guy Carpenter said.

item.title: Update: UK Risk Firm Ambrey Working to Salvage Ship Spewing Oil off Omani Coast
item.description: Risk management firm Ambrey said on Thursday it was coordinating the salvage of a ship spilling Russian crude into the Arabian Sea off the coast of Oman in one of the world’s worst oil spills for years. Ambrey has contracted a “leading international oil spill response company” and is working with Oman and other stakeholders to secure the Caroline Bezengi tanker, it said in a statement. An annual monsoon in the area is complicating the salvage efforts, Ambrey said, a day after Oman confirmed that the massive oil slick from the tanker had reached its shores.

Russia may escalate attacks against the Baltic States and Poland, a European intelligence official said, amid rising concern that Moscow wants to further intimidate nations supporting Ukraine. There are indications that Russian intelligence and security services are looking at so-called hybrid warfare operations, which could include infrastructure sabotage or false-flag attacks, the intelligence official said, declining to be named in order to speak freely.

item.title: Low Rhine River Levels Disrupt German Industry
item.description: German companies are reporting growing disruption from Rhine water levels that have hit record lows, with chemical producers, utilities, steelmakers and agricultural traders warning of higher costs, transport bottlenecks and curbed production. “Alarm bells are ringing loudly: the extremely low water levels are increasingly pushing logistics and supply chains to their limits,” Wolfgang Grosse Entrup, CEO of German chemical industry association VCI, told Reuters. Salzgitter, Germany’s second-largest steelmaker, said that the low Rhine levels had forced it to transport coal via train from Rotterdam to its HKM division.

item.title: Sixfold and Sollers partner to accelerate AI underwriting
item.description: Sixfold has partnered with Sollers Consulting to help insurers accelerate underwriting transformation by combining AI-powered risk assessment with insurance consulting and implementation expertise. Sixfold and Sollers will work with insurers to automate submission intake, assess risks against their own underwriting appetite and generate transparent, explainable recommendations within existing systems and workflows. “Sixfold makes submission handling faster, more consistent and more intelligent,” said Jakub Śliwiński, head of underwriting at Sollers.

item.title: Daisy Tsang to co-lead HSBC insurance business
item.description: The bank plans to appoint  Kai Zhang , Asia head of international wealth and premier banking, and  Daisy Tsang , CEO of HSBC Life Hong Kong and Macau, as co-CEOs of the insurance business alongside their existing roles, according to sources. HSBC’s global head of insurance, Edward Moncreiffe, is set to leave the bank in September after two decades with the lender, as the group continues a broader restructuring and focuses on expanding its wealth business in Asia. Moncreiffe, who has led HSBC’s global insurance business since 2024, is leaving for external opportunities, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Big ‘I’ report shows a stabilizing insurance market
item.description: The Big “I” 2026 Market Share Report shows the independent agency channel continues to maintain control in commercial lines while it is also gaining ground in personal lines. As the insurance market continues to stabilize, the next phase of the market will reward independent agencies that can respond quickly as carriers regain confidence and begin competing for business again. Notably, the independent channel ticked up in personal lines: Personal auto grew from 33% to 34% Homeowners’ insurance grew from 50% to 51% Overall, the market is stable and improving.

item.title: Accelerant to be acquired by Thoma Bravo
item.description: Risk exchange platform Accelerant has entered into a definitive agreement with Thoma Bravo to become a privately held company in an all-cash transaction with an enterprise value of more than $4 billion. Returning to private ownership with Thoma Bravo’s technology and software expertise, coupled with its vast financial and strategic resources, will enable us to make investments that further position our unique, data fueled platform to be the rails on which specialty insurance runs.” – Jeff Radke, Chairman and CEO of Accelerant. Under the terms of the agreement, Accelerant Class A and Class B stockholders will receive $20.25 per share in cash, representing a 49% premium to Accelerant’s closing share price on August 12, 2026.

item.title: Volvo launches new telematics app
item.description: Volvo is introducing Safety Coach, a new telematics app that offers drivers driving insights and tips directly through the infotainment screen and the Volvo Cars mobile app. The tips are guided by findings from Volvo’s “decades-worth of real-world safety knowledge and data,” and the app is powered by Cambridge Mobile Telematics. Starting in Sweden and Norway, drivers of most Volvo cars from model year 2020 can soon download the app.

item.title: Tornado Alley Eastward Shift Adding Risk Concerns, Modeler Says
item.description: The peak of tornado season may be behind us, but the eastward expansion of what has been traditionally known as tornado alley into more populated areas may continue raising awareness of the growing insurance risk long for some time. “The tornado alley’s kind of expanding or shifting a bit eastward, and so I think as we think about that from an insurance perspective and think about ‘What does that mean for insurers,’ I think one of the largest concerns is there’s a lot more population as you move eastward,” said Tory Farney, vice president of Verisk Weather Solutions. Increased losses in new areas weren’t from raw tornado counts across the U.S., but from increased risk exposure, according to one industry catastrophe modeler.

item.title: USDA Says Argentine Beef That Missed Inspection Is Recalled
item.description: The USDA’s Food Safety and Inspection Service announced that Florida-based Corte Argentino LLC was recalling several cuts of beef that missed a “reinspection” step when they entered the US. Nearly 30,000 pounds of Argentine beef that wasn’t fully inspected before being distributed in Texas and Florida are being recalled, the US Department of Agriculture said. The recalled beef cuts came in boxes labeled Frigorifico Gorina SAIC, one of Argentina’s top meatpackers.

item.title: CatIQ finalises loss estimate for Hurricane Debby floods in Ontario & Quebec at C$2.80bn
item.description: CatIQ, the Toronto-based independent catastrophe insurance data provider, has published a final insurance industry loss estimate of CAD $2.80 billion from the severe flooding generated by the remnants of Hurricane Debby that impacted Ontario and Quebec between August 9th and 10th, 2024. Moreover, CatIQ’s final loss estimate is also down from its fourth loss estimate of $2.817 billion, which was issued six months after the event. However, this final estimate is still an increase from CatIQ’s third loss estimate of $2.76 billion, which was issued 90 days after the event took place.

item.title: Suncorp’s exec leadership changes to set insurer for next phase of strategy
item.description: Australian insurer Suncorp Group has announced a number of changes to its executive leadership team, including the appointment of Bridget Messer as Chief Executive Customer, Brand and Digital, a newly created role. As a result of these changes, Michelle Bain, currently Executive General Manager of Compulsory Third Party Insurance will join the Executive Leadership Team as Suncorp’s Chief Risk Officer. She will retain accountability for the rollout of Suncorp’s Digital Insurer program.

item.title: Axle secures $17.5m Series A as insurtech company expands automated platform
item.description: Axle, a technology company developing an AI-native clearinghouse for the insurance industry, has raised USD $17.5 million in Series A funding as it expands its platform for automating insurance verification and policy-related processes. “Axle gives us an instant, accurate answer at the moment it matters and has helped us recover millions in losses we used to write off each year.” Axle’s platform is designed to address what the company describes as a fragmented insurance technology infrastructure. Axle said members of the early Plaid team are among its existing investors.

item.title: HIVE Underwriters strengthens cargo division
item.description: Independent specialty MGA HIVE Underwriters has announced the appointment of Polly Mays as Head of Cargo, bringing a decade of experience in the cargo insurance market, and extensive expertise across cargo, stock throughput, excess stock and project cargo risks. Her appointment further strengthens HIVE’s Marine division as the business continues to expand its underwriting capabilities across global specialty markets. HIVE’s Marine division specialises in technically complex marine risks, including Marine Cargo, Marine Liability, Transportation & Logistics, Marine War and Marine Miscellaneous.
